standard.title: Develop design criteria and evaluate independently
standard.description: develop design criteria independently including sustainability to evaluate design ideas, processes and solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can develop design criteria collaboratively including sustainability to evaluate design ideas, processes and solutions (AC9TDE8P04). They have experience using criteria to guide evaluation. They have not yet developed criteria independently, reflected substantively on process choices, or iterated based on evaluation feedback.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students independently develop design criteria including sustainability and use them to evaluate and iterate design ideas, processes and solutions — including reflecting on process choices and responding creatively to evaluation feedback.

nodes.label: Independently developing design criteria
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can independently develop specific, assessable design criteria that include sustainability considerations.
nodes.minimum_width: Write at least two design criteria independently (without a provided template); criteria must be assessable against a designed solution and include at least one sustainability criterion.
nodes.typical_width: Develop a set of design criteria independently from the design brief — including functional, aesthetic, safety, sustainability and user experience criteria; ensure each criterion is specific and assessable; explain the reasoning behind key criteria choices.
wider: Develop criteria that explicitly specify acceptable performance thresholds (e.g. maximum load for a structure, acceptable stress test result) — not just what is required but how it will be measured
Develop criteria that address the full product life cycle, not just the use phase — including criteria for material sourcing, production impact and end-of-life
Compare criteria developed independently with criteria developed through user consultation — analyse what consultation adds

response_modes.reason: Independent criteria development requires students to reason from the design brief to testable statements. Students who develop criteria without this process produce vague or circular criteria (e.g. 'the product should look good'). The reasoning path (what must this solution do? → how would we know if it did? → what sustainability considerations apply?) produces actionable criteria.

success_criteria: At least two criteria are specific and assessable — a person could check whether a solution meets them
At least one sustainability criterion is included
nodes.hinge_reason: The descriptor specifies criteria developed independently — if students cannot do this at N1, N2 evaluation and N3 reflection are conducted against criteria that are not their own, and the descriptor's core demand is not met.

nodes.label: Evaluating and justifying technology use against criteria
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate and justify the use of traditional, contemporary and emerging technologies during a design project against design criteria including sustainability.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one technology choice made during the project against at least one design criterion; explain whether the choice met the criterion and why.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate and justify technology use across the project — including justification for choosing traditional, contemporary or emerging technologies; apply sustainability criteria to technology choices; evaluate decisions at multiple stages of the project, not just the final solution.
wider: Evaluate and justify farming method choices (e.g. from South-East Asia) against sustainability criteria — explain what the evaluation revealed about the relationship between traditional practice and contemporary sustainability requirements
Compare the sustainability implications of two competing technologies for the same task in the project — make a justified selection and explain what you would trade off
Evaluate whether a technology choice that is superior on performance criteria is inferior on sustainability criteria — make and justify a final decision

response_modes.reason: Technology evaluation against criteria requires students to reason systematically — for each technology choice, does it meet this criterion? why? what trade-off is made? Students who evaluate by intuition produce justifications that cannot ground the specific iterations required at N3.

success_criteria: Evaluation references specific design criteria — not general preferences
Justification explains why the chosen technology meets the criteria better than an alternative
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot evaluate technology choices against criteria at N2 cannot identify what to reflect on and iterate at N3 — reflection without prior evaluation produces generalised commentary rather than specific design improvements.

nodes.label: Reflecting on process and iterating
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on process choices made at various stages of a design process and iterate design ideas to improve outcomes, including sustainability.
nodes.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one process choice made during the project — explain what was decided, whether it was effective, and what you would do differently.
nodes.typical_width: Reflect on learning across the design process — identify choices made at multiple stages that shaped the outcome; evaluate the effectiveness of each; modify plans when needed with reference to design criteria; respond to evaluation feedback by iterating design ideas to improve sustainability or other criteria.
wider: Document and reflect on a full iteration cycle — what feedback prompted the iteration, what was changed, and whether the change improved the solution against the criteria
Reflect on a process choice that prioritised one criterion at the cost of another — evaluate whether the trade-off was justified in hindsight
Use evaluation feedback to explore sustainable material substitutions (e.g. plant-based timber oils, bioplastics) — document the iteration and evaluate the improvement
success_criteria: Reflection identifies a specific process choice — not just a general description of what was done
Reflection includes a judgement about effectiveness and what would be done differently
